components.css: .ds-switch{width:260px;font-family:'Archivo', sans-serif}.ds-labels{position:relative;height:16px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:12px;color:var(--color-text-primary, #241a10)}.ds-labels span{position:absolute;top:0;white-space:nowrap}.ds-l1{left:0}.ds-l2{left:calc(7px + (100% - 14px)/3);transform:translateX(-50%)}.ds-l3{left:calc(7px + (100% - 14px)*2/3);transform:translateX(-50%)}.ds-l4{right:0}.ds-reached{color:var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a);font-weight:700}.ds-track{position:relative;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;height:24px}.ds-fill{position:absolute;top:50%;left:7px;right:7px;height:4px;border-radius:9999px;transform:translateY(-50%);background:linear-gradient(to right,var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a) 0%,var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a) 33%,var(--color-border-subtle, #e0d3ac) 33%,var(--color-border-subtle, #e0d3ac) 100%)}.ds-dot{position:relative;z-index:1;flex:none;width:14px;height:14px;padding:0;border:2px solid var(--color-border-control, #837757);border-radius:9999px;background:var(--color-bg-surface-raised, #fff);cursor:pointer}.ds-dot:hover{border-color:var(--color-text-secondary, #6b6046)}.ds-dot:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--color-focus-ring, #6e2013);outline-offset:2px}.ds-dot-on{border-color:var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a);background:var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a)}.ds-dot-sel::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;z-index:-1;width:18px;height:18px;background:var(--color-accent-selected, #8a2a1a);border-radius:50% 50% 50% 0;transform:translate(-50%,-68%) rotate(-45deg)}.ds-desc{margin:6px 0 0;color:var(--color-text-secondary, #6b6046);font-size:11px;line-height:1.4}

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Scribe's Chronicle"**

O Tempora reads as a chronicle kept by one careful hand: aged parchment for the page, iron-gall ink for every word, and a single oxblood accent standing in for a wax seal. The data is the ornament. Colour, line and dot do the encoding, so chrome stays small, warm and quiet, and nothing competes with the marks on the timeline.

The system is dense but unhurried. Controls are small, pill-shaped and exact; labels are short sentence-case nouns; years are set in tabular figures in the same face as the text around them. Fraunces appears only where a chronicle would letter a heading: the Viewport Range, an entity's name, the wordmark. There is one theme, light, and the system does not ask for a second.
keyCharacteristics: Warm parchment ground with ink text. No pure black, no pure-white page.
One sharp accent (oxblood) reserved for state: selected, reached, primary action.
Colour encodes category within a lane; shape encodes duration (rounded-cap line for a period, dot for a moment), identically in all three lanes.
Tonal layering for depth. Shadows only on cards that float over the canvas.
Quiet and exact controls: hairline borders, 12px type, 28px targets.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: Oxblood marks state and nothing else. It is never decoration and never a lane colour.

rules.name: The Ink Label Rule
rules.body: Entry labels are always Ink, never the mark's colour; the bar or dot alone carries the category.

rules.name: The Fixed Legend Rule
rules.body: The eight People domains render in the order listed above. Reordering re-opens the colour-blind adjacency checks.

rules.name: The Border Ladder Rule
rules.body: An interactive control's border is Control Border. Hairline and Strong Rule never border a control.

rules.name: The Same Face Rule
rules.body: Years and dates use Archivo with tabular figures, never a separate monospace.

rules.name: The Three Headings Rule
rules.body: Fraunces is for the Viewport Range, the entity name and the wordmark. Chrome stays in Archivo.

rules.name: The Floaters-Only Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only if it sits over the canvas. Everything inline is separated by tone and hairlines.

rules.name: The Halo Rule
rules.body: A selected or search-jumped mark gets a duplicate shape in Selection Halo, 8px wider than the grown mark, drawn behind it. The mark itself is never recoloured.

dos: **Do** use Ink for text and every entry label, and Faded Ink for secondary text; both pass 4.5:1 on every surface they sit on.
**Do** border interactive controls with Control Border (#837757) and step hover to Faded Ink.
**Do** give every interactive control a 2px Deep Oxblood focus outline with a 1–2px offset (negative inside joined groups).
**Do** keep chrome type at 12px or larger where it is not data; 10–11px is for ticks, badges and lane labels only.
**Do** use tabular figures for every year and date.
**Do** keep marks at least 3:1 against parchment at resting opacity; check any new mark colour against the existing set, not just its neighbour.
**Do** use text glyphs (`×`, `+`, `−`, `«`) for tight controls.
donts: **Don't** use oxblood as a lane colour, a decoration, or a hover tint.
**Don't** recolour a selected mark; add the halo.
**Don't** colour entry labels with their mark's colour.
**Don't** add a dark theme or a second accent.
**Don't** use gradients, imagery or emoji in chrome, or exclamation marks and marketing voice in copy.
**Don't** add a shadow to an inline surface or a border to a control in Hairline or Strong Rule.
**Don't** introduce an icon set or a monospace face.
